title: Rank of Each Person in a Stream
statement:
People arrive one at a time, and person `i` has an integer strength `s[i]`. As each person arrives (moving left to right), you must report that person's **rank** among everyone who has arrived so far, including the person themselves.

The rank is defined as `1 +` the number of **earlier** people whose strength is **strictly greater** than the current person's. The strongest person so far therefore has rank `1`, and people with equal strength share the same rank (a tie never pushes someone down).

For every person, output their rank at the moment they arrive. The whole stream fits in memory, so you may read all of it first.

**Follow-up:** the interviewer asked for the solution to be built on your own binary search tree, augmented so every node stores the size of its subtree, instead of a library ordered set. Any structure that gives the right answers passes the tests here.
inputFormat:
The first line contains an integer `n`.
The second line contains `n` space-separated integers `s[0], s[1], ..., s[n - 1]`.
outputFormat: Print `n` space-separated integers: the rank of each person at the time of arrival.

examples.explanation: Time 0: only 5 is present, so its rank is 1. Time 1: among [5, 4], 4 has one stronger person (5), so rank 2. Time 2: 6 is stronger than both 5 and 4, so rank 1. Time 3: all of 5, 4, 6 are stronger than 1, so rank 4.

2 is first (rank 1). 7 has no stronger person before it (rank 1). The second 7 ties with the first, so it is also rank 1. The second 2 has two stronger people (7, 7), so rank 3. 9 is the strongest (rank 1). The last 7 has only the 9 stronger, so rank 2.

hints: Rank only depends on how many earlier values are strictly greater, so the question at each step is a 'count of elements greater than x among those inserted so far'.
A balanced BST where each node stores its subtree size, or a Fenwick tree over compressed values, answers that count and supports inserting the new value in O(log n).
Count earlier values that are <= x (or > x) with a prefix query, then rank = (number inserted so far) - (count <= x) + 1. Remember equal values must not be counted as stronger.
